title: .dev-workflow/verification-recipe.json
description: The one artifact the tier derivation emits: tier + dimension preset + hard floors from one input set, so depth and rubric never decouple. Produced downstream by the derive script /aep-e2e-skill-scaffolding scaffolds, whose emitter is the source of truth this schema follows. Read by /aep-launch (evaluator existence + criteria policy), /aep-build Phase 5 (binding tier), and the autopilot's tier-aware nudges via status.json. Tamper rule: the binding derivation only ratchets UP from the provisional tier, and customization may add dimensions or raise floors, never lower them.

base_sha.description: The resolved $BASE commit the diff was taken against

tier.description: The binding tier. Absent provisional input fails OPEN to deep — never to a default.

tier_provisional.description: The tier the dispatch brief carried in; binding only ratchets up from it

tier_escalated.description: Deprecated: always false. There is no standard → deep auto-escalation; the field is kept so recipes and consumers that carry it still validate

scope_drift.description: The binding diff left the declared files_affected

referee_assets_touched.description: Tests/journeys/gates touched — never derives light; floors at standard

negative_assertion_delta.description: More assertions removed than added; always forces at least one evaluation round

hard_floors.description: Dimension name → minimum score on the 0–4 scale. Keys come from the preset (scoring-framework.md); customization may add keys or raise values, never remove or lower.

max_rounds.description: Eval-round cap for the binding tier (light 0; standard and deep 2; a negative assertion delta raises 0 to 1). A recipe carrying a larger number does not raise the cap — the protocol cap of 2 governs (eval-protocol.md)

evaluator_effort.description: Effort pinned on every evaluator spawn. none is the light tier (no evaluator spawns); default and highest are deprecated aliases of high

inputs.description: The derivation's raw inputs, kept for audit — why this recipe says what it says
